events.feedback:
This draft for the Pomegranate (Punica granatum) is wonderfully evocative. The historical connection between the fruit's old French name (pomme grenade) and the word "grenade" is a brilliant linguistic nugget that visitors will love sharing.

Because South Florida’s climate can be tricky for this ancient fruit, here are a few tailored observations to ensure this profile is completely air-tight before you publish:

🌟 Why it works
Spot-on Taxonomy: Correctly placing it in the Lythraceae family (loosestrife family) shows great attention to detail, as it was historically placed in its own family (Punicaceae).

Accurate Fruit Morphology: Properly defining the edible portion as the aril rather than just calling it a "seed" is exactly the kind of educational precision a botanical park should feature.

🔧 Tweaks for the West Coast Florida Context
The Reality of Fruiting in Bradenton (Crucial Context): You appropriately noted in the origin section that it "fruits best where summers are drier" an
